A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TT-Occ and contain readable main text, equations, Tables 1–6, Figures 1–12, and Appendices A–B. The complete material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original occupancy-prediction experiments on Occ3D-nuScenes and nuCraft, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and appendix robustness evaluations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark accuracy, ablations, and appendix evaluations, and revises several efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same Gaussian initialization, RAFT-based camera motion masking, DBSCAN/ICP LiDAR tracking, covariance-aware voxelization, and optional TRBF smoothing. No algorithm or objective changes are documented.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Occ3D-nuScenes at 0.4 m and nuCraft at 0.2 m, with camera and LiDAR variants. Appendix B.1 retains the same five rainy/nighttime nuScenes scenes; no dataset, task, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding experiments, including Table 1's occupancy methods, SelfOcc and C-CONet in Table 2, and SelfOcc in Tables 3, 4, and 6. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The stated validation evaluation, 10% component-ablation subset, class exclusions, mIoU/RayIoU metrics, and OpenSeeD-controlled comparison remain unchanged. The newly disclosed GPU and removal of Table 4's split specification concern documentation; neither establishes an altered experimental procedure.

E4.justification: Figure 5's component ablations, Table 4's VFM comparisons, Table 6's adverse-weather tests, and Appendix B.2's expanded ablation/TRBF visualizations retain the same questions, comparisons, and evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version provides experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The reporting practices for averages remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 1 revises TT-OccLiDAR from 1.9 to 2.3 FPS, and Table 5 revises its peak memory from 8.5 to 5.6 GB. Figure 6 reduces semantic extraction from approximately 420 to 310 ms, shortening both variants' runtime bars. Accuracy, ablation, and robustness scores remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain the efficiency revisions or establish their cause.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(6), TRBF kernel reasoning, and appendix optical-flow relation are unchanged. Equation (5) moves between pages without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The central claims remain training-free test-time occupancy prediction, flexible voxel resolution, open-vocabulary semantics, temporal consistency, and competitive efficiency. v4's abstract explicitly states superiority over pretrained counterparts, but v3 already makes that claim in its introduction and results.

C2.justification: Both retain the explanations for tracking, metric-depth benefits, and VFM modularity, alongside limitations involving LiDAR sparsity, camera depth/flow noise, and occlusion. Rewording does not introduce a substantive interpretation or limitation.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-repository link and specifies an NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada (48 GB) GPU, neither disclosed in v3. Appendix implementation details remain unchanged. Conversely, Table 4 drops its explicit full-validation-set designation without specifying a replacement split.

R1.justification: v4 adds three introductory citations: Revisiting Domain-Adaptive 3D Object Detection, DPO, and DiVER. The substantive positioning against occupancy-prediction and driving-scene reconstruction methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 shortens and rewrites the abstract, lightly edits explanatory paragraphs, changes appendix references to supplementary-material references, and adds acknowledgments and affiliation/corresponding-author details. The scientific section order and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: The runtime plots are resized and updated, Figure 3's image crops change, and several captions and table layouts are adjusted. Table 6 gains a Scene ID header and full variant names. Page numbers disappear and text reflows, but no figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The code link and hardware specification improve reproducibility disclosure. However, revised Figure 6 implies semantic-processing shares of approximately 22.7% and 72.3%, while the text retains v3's 28.5% and 77.9%. Table 4 also loses its full-validation-set clarification. With scientific accuracy evidence unchanged, these documentation gains and reporting regressions leave the net quality direction unclear.
